records.name: CSV User Import
records.description: Happy path for importing users (or leads) into Intercom from a CSV file. Entry: user opens the Import data modal from the Contacts area and chooses the CSV importer. The flow guides the user to upload a file, map CSV columns to Intercom attributes (email is required), optionally add tags, then start the import. The import runs in the background and the final screen shows import results and any errors. Assumptions: user is authenticated and has access to Contacts and importer features; this is a desktop browser flow.
records.problem:
User goal: Add or update people in Intercom by uploading a CSV so that contacts exist in the platform with proper attributes and optional tags. The user expects a guided, step-by-step import (upload → map columns → add tags → import) and clear feedback if rows fail.

Interface perspective: The UI provides a modal launcher, a multi-step import wizard (Upload CSV → Map attributes → Tag → Import), inline previews of CSV columns for mapping, a lightweight modal for mapping a selected column to a named attribute, a tag picker to attach tags to the import, and status screens showing processing and final results. At the end the user sees counts (created/updated/errors) and an errors table with row, column and error type.

Result: User-perceived outcome: CSV is submitted and processed; user sees successful import or a list of errors to correct. System-level outcome: Intercom creates or updates user records for valid rows, applies mapped attributes and tags, and records import errors for invalid rows (example shown: invalid email entries).

Interface/system perspective: The UI provides a multi-step modal: file selection -> column mapping with auto-map and manual selection -> mapping review -> start import. It enforces required/ preferred fields via messaging and validation indicators, shows sample values to help the user verify mappings, and displays a processing notification when import begins. Result at the end: user-perceived outcome — the UI confirms the CSV was uploaded and that contact creation is being processed; system-level outcome — the CSV file is accepted, column mappings are stored, and the backend begins creating or updating contact records (processing indicated by a toast).

content.description:
Overall style and purpose:
- Clean, modern enterprise / SaaS CRM workspace with a two-column split: a left conversational/notes panel driven by an AI assistant and a right contacts management panel. Visual language is neutral, minimal, product-focused: lots of white space, light greys, subtle dividers and rounded corners. The look-and-feel matches systems using Inter/Roboto-like geometric sans fonts, thin dividers, and small iconography.

Color palette (approximate HEX):
- Page background: very light grey #F6F7F8
- Panel / card background: white #FFFFFF
- Primary text (headings): near-black #111827
- Body text: dark grey #374151
- Muted text / secondary: #6B7280
- Divider / input border: #E5E7EB
- Row hover / subtle surface: #F3F4F6
- Primary accent (links / interactive): blue #2563EB
- Success/online status dot: bright green #10B981
- Button border / subtle accents: #D1D5DB

Typography (recommended to match screenshot):
- Font family: Inter or System UI (Helvetica/Arial fallback)
- Headline / Section title: 16-18px, 600 (semibold), line-height ~22px
- Item title (contact name): 14-15px, 600, line-height 20px
- Body / metadata (role, email): 12-13px, 400-500, line-height 16-18px
- Small / helper text (timestamps, hints): 11-12px, 400

Layout and spacing:
- Two main columns: left column ~62-66% width, right column ~34-38% width, with a 20-24px gutter between.
- Left column: top header area (title / context), then a vertically stacked set of content blocks (AI-generated message cards / paragraphs). Each content block is a white card on the left panel with 16px internal padding and 8-16px spacing between paragraphs/elements. At the bottom of the left column a fixed composer / input bar (height ~56px) spans the column, with rounded input, an action chip for account selection at left, and subtle action icons at right.
- Right column: vertically divided into header controls and content list. Header contains a horizontal tab strip (All, Tracking, Engaged) left-aligned, and an Add Contact button with a chevron/dropdown at the right of the header. Below header is a search + filter row (search field with icon left, filter button right). The main content is a vertical list/table of contacts where each row contains a left checkbox, avatar, contact name (bold), role/title (small), and email on the right with a small status indicator (green dot). Rows are compact, ~56-72px height, with subtle dividing lines between rows.
- Sidebar: a narrow left vertical navbar with rounded icons stacked vertically. The top of the page shows a compact top toolbar with a small title (OpenAI Project Creat...) and close icon (X) in top-right of the viewport.

UI element details and sizes:
- Left message cards: width = left column width minus 32px padding; border-radius 8px; padding 16px; subtle drop shadow (0 1px 2px rgba(16,24,40,0.03)).
- Composer / Input field: full-width rounded rectangle, height ~48-56px, inner padding 12px, placeholder text grey (#9CA3AF). Contains inline account chip (rounded pill ~32px height, 12px horizontal padding) to indicate selected account (label: "OpenAI"). There is a subtle helper line under the composer explaining usage.
- Tabs: small segmented control; active tab uses primary accent (#2563EB) underline or bold text; inactive tabs muted (#6B7280).
- Add Contact button: outline/ghost button with label and down chevron. Button height 36px, border 1px #D1D5DB, background #FFFFFF, border-radius 8px. Dropdown menu uses a white popover with slight elevation (box-shadow) and items: Manual, With LinkedIn Url, Add via CSV. Popover animation: 120ms scale/opacity with ease-out.
- Search Field: rounded input, height ~36px, left search icon, placeholder "Search"; border #E5E7EB; on focus border changes to accent #2563EB with subtle shadow.
- List row composition: checkbox (24px) on left, avatar circle 36px, name (14px semibold) with optional small icons next to name, role/title in 12px muted grey under or next to name, email on right in 12px muted, status green dot near email. Row hover highlight: background #F3F4F6.
- Icons: line-style, 16-20px size; use neutral color #6B7280.

States & interactions / micro-interactions:
- Hover states: rows and buttons show slightly darker background / border; buttons show 120-160ms color transitions.
- Dropdown/popover: scale from 0.98 to 1 and opacity from 0% to 100% in 100-140ms ease-out.
- Tabs: click switches content instantly; active tab indicator animates with 120ms ease.
- Search: instant filter of visible list rows (client-side) with a subtle “no results” empty state illustration if none.

Accessibility & affordances:
- Clear focus outlines on keyboard focus for inputs and list rows.
- Sufficient color contrast on primary text (#111827) vs white and muted text at smaller sizes uses 12-13px with sufficient contrast.

Recreating notes to designer:
- Use a two-column responsive grid with a flexible left column (min-width 540px) and a fixed-ish right column (300-420px). Left column must allow long prose and AI-generated content blocks; right column must be a scrollable list independent of the left column scroll (sticky header for search/tabs optional).
- Use a narrow left icon bar separate from main columns: keep icons vertically centered with equal spacing and subtle hover backgrounds.
- Use a consistent 8px spacing scale for padding & gaps.
- Keep all dropdowns and popovers anchored to the triggering button with 8px offset and slight corner radius 8px.

Assets & icons to include when recreating:
- Avatars (circular), checkbox, search magnifier, filter funnel, chevron-down, inline mention @ icon, green status dot, small role/flag icons.

Animation summary:
- Popover open/close: 100-140ms scale & fade (ease-out cubic).
- Row hover: 80-120ms background color transition (ease-in-out).
- Active tab underline slide: 150ms ease.

This description should allow another designer to closely reproduce the two-column CRM + assistant interface shown in the screenshot.

- Modal title: 18–20px, 600–700 weight (semibold), line-height ~1.2, left aligned inside card header

The dropzone may show a subtle dashed border or a faint inner stroke (#E6E9EE). Dropzone dimensions visually: ~260–360px wide x ~160–220px tall depending on modal width.

Left screen (background content):

- Body group (dropzone card) — centered block with top/bottom padding; dropzone content vertically stacked: icon, primary instruction, secondary hint.

- Click the dropzone area to open the native file selector and choose a CSV file.
- Drag a CSV file over the dropzone to trigger a drag-over state and drop to upload.

High-level goals (why user uses this screen):
- Allow users to quickly bulk-add contacts into the product by uploading a CSV file with minimal friction and clear guidance about required fields.

content.description:
Centered modal dialog titled "Map your columns" over a dimmed page overlay. The modal uses a light card with subtle rounded corners and a faint shadow; the overlay behind is a semi-opaque neutral gray (approx. rgba(0,0,0,0.35)). Top-left of the modal shows the title in a bold, medium-large sans-serif (approx. 18-20px, 600 weight). Under the title a two-line descriptive paragraph (13-14px, regular weight, #6b7280 / cool gray) explains mapping priority and guidance.

Directly under the description is a horizontal controls row with three small tab/pill options: "All" (active), "Mapped" (count) and an "Auto-map" button styled like a secondary control. To the right of these controls is a compact search field with a magnifier icon and placeholder text (approx. 14px). The main content area is a two-column layout inside the modal body with a subtle divider between columns.

Left/main column (approx. 65% width of modal) contains the mapping table: a header row labels two columns "CSV Column (2 of 2)" and "Rox Field". Under that are two horizontal rows, each representing a CSV column. Each row has the CSV column name in a small pill/label on the left (light gray background #f3f4f6, 13-14px, medium weight). To the right of each CSV label is a right-arrow chevron and then a dropdown control (wide, rounded 6px, light border #e5e7eb) containing the text "Select field". Dropdown caret icon on the right of the control. Row spacing is generous (row height ~56px) and each row has a very light bottom divider. The left column background is pure white (#ffffff) with 20-24px internal padding.

Right/preview column (approx. 35% width) contains a vertically stacked list of sample values with a small caption above "Sample values from CSV" (12-13px, muted gray). Each sample value (e.g., "Liam Carter", "Sofia Bennett", etc.) is presented in its own bordered row with subtle divider lines and left-aligned text (14px, #111827). The sample list is scrollable if items exceed the visible height. The right column has the same white background and matching padding; the divider between left and right is a 1px subtle line (#e6e6e6).

Top-right corner of the modal shows a small close icon (X) in muted gray. Bottom-right of the modal footer contains two navigation buttons: "Previous" (left) styled as a subdued outline/ghost button with a small left-arrow icon, and "Next Step" (right) styled as a primary rounded button. In the screenshot the "Next Step" is visually disabled/low-emphasis (light gray) indicating inactive state — the primary affordance is placed here but inactive until fields are mapped. Buttons are about 36-40px tall with 12-16px horizontal padding. The footer area has ~18px padding and the modal interior uses consistent 20px to 28px gutters.

Visual style summary: modern, minimal, neutral product UI — lots of white space, cool-gray muted helper text, subtle borders and shadows. Approximate color palette: background overlay rgba(0,0,0,0.35); modal background #FFFFFF; primary text #111827; secondary/muted text #6B7280; dividers and form borders #E5E7EB / #E6E6E6; input background / pills #F3F4F6; primary button (active) hypothetical brand blue #2563EB; disabled button #F3F4F6 with text #9CA3AF. Typography appears to be a clean geometric sans (system/Inter-like) with sizes: title 18-20px 600, body/fields 13-14px 400, labels 12-13px 500.

Micro-interactions / states: dropdowns show an inactive placeholder state and on hover transition border color from #E5E7EB to #D1D5DB with a 120ms ease. Active/selected dropdown shows accent border (brand color). Tabs/pills show an active background (white) with subtle underline or bolder text. Hover states for rows highlight with a faint background tint (#FAFAFB). Sample list scroll uses native scrollbars or thin custom track in light gray. The close icon has a hover state of slightly darker gray. The disabled Next Step button reduces opacity to 50% and disables pointer events.

Overall the dialog is a mapping wizard step for importing a CSV and assigning CSV columns to internal data fields with live sample preview.
content.layout:
Modal / centered overlay layout. The modal itself is a single container subdivided vertically into three main zones: header (title + description + controls), content (two-column body), and footer (navigation buttons). The content area uses a two-column grid: left column (mapping area) and right column (sample values preview). Column proportions: left ~65% (mapping table and controls), right ~35% (sample list). Within the left column the mapping table is a two-column internal structure: column A shows CSV Column labels (stacked rows), column B shows corresponding target field dropdowns. Rows are stacked vertically; in the screenshot there are 2 mapping rows (name, email). The right column is a single vertical list (one column, approx 10 sample rows visible). The modal width is wide (approx 1000-1300px on desktop) with 24px internal padding. Footer contains two buttons aligned to the right (Previous to left of Next Step). Keywords to describe layout: centered modal, overlay, two-column grid, mapping table, right-side preview, header controls, footer nav, stacked rows, dropdowns, scrollable list.
content.functions:
Specific actions available on this screen:
- Read the header and description to understand mapping priority and recommended fields.
- Use the search field to filter CSV column names or suggested internal fields.
- Click a CSV row to focus it; click the dropdown labeled "Select field" to open a list of available target fields and choose one. The dropdown provides a filtered list as you type.
- Use the "Auto-map" control to attempt automatic field matching based on column names (e.g., name -> Full Name, email -> Email).
- Inspect sample values in the right column to verify whether the selected mapping matches expected data formats (e.g., single full name, email patterns).
- Close the dialog with the X in the top-right corner to cancel mapping.
- Navigate between steps using the footer controls: "Previous" to go back, "Next Step" to proceed once required mappings are completed. "Next Step" is disabled until necessary mappings are made.

Medium-level tasks and workflows:
- Complete a CSV import workflow: upload CSV (previous step), map CSV columns to system fields (this step), validate preview values and proceed to import/enrich data (next step).
- Correct mapping mistakes by changing dropdown selections or using auto-map to reassign multiple columns quickly.
- Validate that imported contacts will have correct attributes by scanning sample values to detect misaligned columns (e.g., emails in name column).

Broader user goal enabled by this screen:
- The user prepares and verifies data before importing to the system, ensuring accurate enrichment and correct field attribution. This reduces import errors, improves data quality, and allows the system to attach enriched contact metadata (LinkedIn, company website, etc.) to the correct fields. The interface is designed to be clear and efficient, letting users map many columns quickly (via auto-map or search) while confirming results via sample previews.

content.description:
Overall style: A neutral, professional modal/dialog interface for mapping CSV columns to internal fields. The modal sits on top of a dimmed/blurred background and uses a light, minimal design with subtle shadows, rounded corners, and a mostly monochrome grayscale palette with restrained accents. Visual language is system UI/Inter-like: compact, readable, high information density and clear micro-interactions (dropdowns, search, tabs).

Container and background:

- Modal container: centered, large horizontal rectangle with rounded corners (6-10px radius), subtle drop shadow (0 10px 30px rgba(16,24,40,0.12)). Background of modal: near-white (#FFFFFF) with a light grey border or subtle inner shadow to separate from overlay.

Main content layout (three-column grid):

Specific actions (per-row and per-component):
- Search contacts: user clicks into the search input, types a query; results filter in real time or after hitting Enter. The UI provides a clear placeholder and search icon for affordance.
- Filter contacts: user taps the Filter button to open a filter panel (dropdown or modal) where they can toggle attributes like engagement status, tags, or tracking status; filtering updates the list.
- Switch tabs: user clicks tabs (All / Tracking / Engaged) to change the subset of contacts shown. The active tab visually highlights with an underline and bolder text.
- Select contacts: user checks the checkbox at the start of a row to select single or multiple contacts for bulk actions (delete, export, add to list). A bulk actions bar may appear when rows are selected.
- Add contact: user clicks the "Add Contact" primary button which opens a modal or side-sheet form to input name, email, role, tags and save to the contacts database.
- Open contact details: clicking a row (or an avatar/name) opens the contact profile in a right-side detail pane or separate modal, allowing edits, notes, or activity view.
- Upload CSV: user can upload a CSV to bulk add contacts. During upload, a toast or status card appears with progress information; when complete, the list is refreshed to include new contacts.
- Row actions: hover on a row reveals contextual actions (ellipsis menu) such as edit, message, delete, or view activity; these actions provide instant contextual affordances.
- Presence/status readouts: green status dot indicates online/presence; email addresses are visible and copyable on click or via an inline action.

Medium-level tasks / workflows:
- Adding a new contact manually: click Add Contact → fill the modal form → save → contact is added and appears in the list with a short success toast.
- Bulk import: click upload/import → choose CSV → observe upload progress toast → confirm mapping of CSV columns (name, email, role) if required → finish → contacts updated and optionally selected.
- Filtering and outreach: select a subset via tabs + filter + search → check multiple rows → trigger bulk action (e.g., send email, export, or tag), enabling efficient outreach.
- Quick lookup and copy: search for a person → hover/click to reveal actions → copy email or open full profile for contact-specific interactions.

Broader goals enabled by this interface:
- Manage and maintain a contact database for an organization: add, import, search, tag, and filter contacts efficiently.
- Rapidly find and act on contacts for customer outreach or account management workflows (track engagement, mark tracked or engaged, and perform bulk operations).
- Integrate contact operations with content/editor workflows: the left editor suggests context-aware usage (e.g., referencing or messaging contacts while drafting notes) so users can combine content creation with contact management in one screen.

How the screen supports these goals:
- Clear separation of concerns with a persistent right-hand contacts column allows users to reference contact data without leaving the primary content/editor area.
- Search, tabs, and filters provide fast discovery and segmentation.
- Per-row affordances (checkboxes, contextual menus, avatars) make single and bulk workflows efficient.
- CSV upload and toast feedback streamline mass updates and provide immediate feedback to the user.
